baseline_models.focus_anchor: The doubled ن ه ي at words 5 and 11 encloses ن ج و at 7 and 13, with ع و د at 9 carrying the group back across the prohibition.
baseline_models.mechanism: A forbidden private channel becomes reciprocal practice: prohibition is stated, the group returns, and the noun for counsel reappears as their mutual act. Sin delays movement toward good, aggression crosses a limit, and disobedience fixes the cell against the Messenger, so the verse depicts organized recurrence rather than a stray whisper.

activation_trace.role: The stopping and restraining branch supplies the twice-marked boundary that the group re-enters.
The secret-counsel branch supplies the separated conversational channel that becomes reciprocal in يتناجون.
The habit and continuance branch turns return from a single relapse into practiced recurrence.
The limit-crossing branch states the normative work performed by the recurring cell.
Departure from obedience fixes the repeated counsel against the Messenger's command.

changed_reading.before: A group commits an isolated act of forbidden whispering.
changed_reading.after: A private counter-cell repeatedly reconstitutes itself by crossing a stated boundary and rehearsing disobedience as a group habit.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: ح ي ي at words 20 and 23 marks an outward greeting, while ق و ل at 26 and ن ف س at 28 introduce a second utterance kept within themselves.
baseline_models.mechanism: The life-and-peace force of greeting is retained as social form but detached from the divine greeting named as its measure. The same visitors then operate an inward speech channel, so the encounter is split between a public salutation and a concealed taunt about punishment.

activation_trace.role: The greeting as a wish for life and peace supplies the benign public form that is being counterfeited.
The branch of saying what is not so sharpens the mismatch between their salutation and the divine template.
Unvoiced saying supplies the concealed verbal channel behind the public greeting.
What resides in inward thought locates the taunt in a hidden deliberative space.

changed_reading.before: The visitors offer an offensive greeting and privately think something defiant.
changed_reading.after: They stage a two-channel speech act: a life-bearing social form masks an inward challenge to the authority that defines a true greeting.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The inward question at words 29-33 demands immediate ع ذ ب, but ح س ب at 34, ص ل ي at 36, and ص ي ر at 38 answer with sufficiency, fire-contact, and destination.
baseline_models.mechanism: They treat the absence of immediate punishment as evidence against accountability. The verse does not accept their timing test; it answers with a punishment already sufficient for them and a destination they will enter, shifting the scale from instant retaliation to settled outcome.

activation_trace.role: The inward-speech branch carries the group's private test of whether their words have consequences.
The pain-and-penalty branch supplies the immediate sanction they demand as proof.
The sufficiency branch supplies the decisive countermeasure: Hell alone is enough for them.
Contact with fire converts abstract sufficiency into experienced consequence.
The becoming-and-outcome branch relocates judgment from their preferred instant to the settled end.

changed_reading.before: The closing threat simply appends a future punishment to their present mockery.
changed_reading.after: The close directly defeats their impunity test: delayed response is not failed authority because a sufficient and settled outcome already answers their calculation.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same return construction serves two opposite recurrence patterns. At 58:3 return to prior speech opens an interrupting sequence of release before renewed contact; at 58:8 return runs directly back into the forbidden reciprocal act. The focus group's defining failure is therefore not recurrence alone but recurrence without repair.

activation_trace.role: Restraint supplies the breached command around the focus return.
Habitual return supplies the focus group's uninterrupted relapse.
Return after a prior act supplies the close syntactic parallel whose continuation introduces repair.

structural_cues: 58:3 and 58:8 repeat ثم يعودون لما; 58:3 then inserts expiation before contact, whereas 58:8 proceeds into ويتناجون.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated construction and different continuations; I infer that the missing repair interval in 58:8 marks willful maintenance of the cycle. A live alternative is that the parallel marks recurrence only, without an intended repair contrast.

changed_reading.after: They choose a repairless mode of return, unlike the nearby return whose consequences interrupt repetition before renewed relation.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus triad moves from crossing a limit to leaving obedience, while the context names God's boundaries and repeatedly describes opposition to God and Messenger with the same boundary root. Their counsel functions as a counter-border: a private enclave organized on the far side of a publicly marked limit.

activation_trace.role: The endpoint branch gives the prohibition a spatially legible limit.
Crossing a boundary supplies the movement by which the counsel becomes aggression.
Exit from obedience identifies which side of the limit the group occupies.
The distinguishing barrier branch supplies the named divine boundaries around the focus behavior.
The opposition branch turns boundary placement into active counter-positioning against God and Messenger.
The repeated opposition branch confirms that this counter-position frames the later factional material as well.

structural_cues: 58:4 names حدود الله; 58:5 and 58:20 repeat يحادون الله ورسوله around the focus and later faction sequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies limits, crossing, disobedience, and repeated counter-positioning; I infer a social border-making mechanism in the private group. The alternative is a purely juridical description with no enclave geometry.

changed_reading.before: Their counsel contains several kinds of wrongdoing.
changed_reading.after: The counsel is an organized counter-jurisdiction that repeatedly places its members across the God-and-Messenger boundary.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context moves from divine hearing, through exhaustive counting and witnessed presence, to knowledge inside every secret council. What the speakers treat as an enclosed channel is epistemically open and preservable; even their unvoiced challenge becomes material that can be returned to them as an account.

activation_trace.role: Hidden saying supplies the speech the group assumes has no external audience.
Secret counsel supplies the enclosure whose epistemic failure is exposed by context.
Perception of sound establishes that speech addressed within human limits is heard by God.
Exhaustive enumeration supplies preservation precise enough to oppose human forgetting.
Presence with observation turns knowledge into witnessed accountability.
Disclosure to the knower removes any epistemic enclosure from the secret council.
The same secret-counsel branch directly places divine knowledge within the group's chosen channel.

structural_cues: 58:1 opens with speech heard; 58:6 says God counted what they forgot; 58:7 places God with every council and says their acts will be reported back.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies hearing, counting, witnessing, knowledge, and later notification; I infer a transcript-like conversion of hidden speech into evidence. The alternative is omniscience without any implied record mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Secret counsel and inward speech hide the group's intent from other people.
changed_reading.after: Their privacy architecture becomes an involuntary evidentiary channel: concealed speech is heard, counted, witnessed, and eventually narrated back.

context_deltas.mechanism: 58:9 preserves reciprocal private counsel while replacing its governing contents. The channel can carry sin, aggression, and disobedience, or expansive good and protective God-consciousness; its ethical charge comes from what the separated group coordinates and where that coordination leads.

activation_trace.role: Secret counsel supplies the medium initially fused with the hostile triad.
Delay from good supplies one destructive payload of the focus counsel.
Limit-crossing supplies a second destructive payload rather than an essence of privacy.
Repeated secret counsel preserves the same medium while the command changes its content.
Expansive goodness and obedience supply a positive cargo for the same reciprocal channel.
Placing oneself under protection gives the positive counsel a self-limiting orientation.

structural_cues: 58:9 repeats the focus triad after فلا تتناجوا, then coordinates وتناجوا with البر والتقوى and a gathering horizon.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the unchanged counsel construction with opposed complements; I infer that privacy is a morally indexable medium, not intrinsically illicit. The alternative is narrower: the verse regulates believer conduct without making a general claim about the medium.

changed_reading.before: Secret counsel is itself the corrupt practice condemned in 58:8.
changed_reading.after: The corrupt practice is a private coordination channel loaded with boundary-crossing content; the same channel can be redirected toward good and protective restraint.

context_deltas.mechanism: 58:10 distinguishes designed effect from actual efficacy. Hostile counsel aims to roughen believers' inner state with grief, but its capacity to inflict loss is bounded; the focus group's visible clustering and coded greeting can therefore operate as intimidation even when they cannot deliver the harm they imply.

activation_trace.role: The concealed reciprocal channel supplies the observable social formation used by the hostile group.
The distorted peace-greeting supplies a public signal capable of carrying menace while retaining social form.
The same secret-counsel branch is explicitly assigned an affective purpose in context.
Inner roughness through grief supplies the intended injury produced by the display of counsel.
Loss opposed to benefit supplies the materially bounded harm that the counsel cannot independently secure.

structural_cues: 58:10 uses a purpose clause, ليحزن, and immediately negates independent harm with وليس بضارهم شيئا.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies intended grief and bounded harm; I infer that the focus clustering and greeting function as social intimidation. A live alternative is that the grief is wholly inward or spiritual, without a public signaling mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The council is mainly a hidden place where plans are exchanged.
changed_reading.after: It is also an affective weapon: the group performs concealed coordination to make believers feel threatened, while its implied power exceeds its actual capacity to harm.

context_deltas.mechanism: Private access to the Messenger is not abolished; it is preceded by an outward transfer that is called better and purer. This adds friction and public benefit before exclusive speech, contrasting with the focus group's costless enclosure and disobedient access.

activation_trace.role: Secret counsel supplies the unaccountable private channel used against the Messenger in the focus.
Private counsel with the Messenger preserves the channel under a different access rule.
Advancing something beforehand supplies the threshold that must precede private access.
A transferred charitable right externalizes benefit before the private exchange.
Purifying conduct supplies the stated effect of placing that threshold before counsel.

structural_cues: 58:12 places charity before نجوى الرسول and calls the sequence better and purer; 58:13 relaxes the charge but restores shared duties and obedience.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a prior charitable transfer and purification; I infer that this friction checks capture, frivolity, or exclusivity by externalizing a cost. The alternative is devotional preparation alone, without an institutional access-control function.

changed_reading.before: The focus suggests that privacy around the Messenger is inherently suspect.
changed_reading.after: Privacy is legitimate when made answerable to an outward threshold and common good; 58:8 condemns captured, costless privacy organized in disobedience.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later oath sequence exposes a reusable strategy: a conventional public utterance is made false and then used as protection. Read back into 58:8, the malformed greeting is not only abuse; it can be a social credential that lets concealed hostility approach under cover.

activation_trace.role: The peace-greeting branch supplies the conventional public credential presented on arrival.
Hidden saying supplies the hostile interior that the credential conceals.
The oath branch supplies a later conventional speech act deployed despite known falsity.
Contradiction of truth separates the public verbal form from the speaker's knowledge.
The protective-cover branch makes explicit the defensive function of the false public utterance.

structural_cues: 58:14 joins oath, lie, and knowledge; 58:16 states that the oaths were taken as a protective cover.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies false oaths functioning as cover; I transfer that speech-shield mechanism to the focus greeting because it likewise fronts concealed hostility. The alternative is that the greeting is pure insult, not a credential for access.

changed_reading.before: The greeting merely insults the Messenger while their real thought stays private.
changed_reading.after: The greeting may also function as verbal cover, preserving access and social deniability for a hostile inward program.

context_deltas.mechanism: Three measures collide: worldly holdings cannot suffice, the speakers reckon that they stand on something, and Hell is sufficient for them. The focus answer is thus exact counter-accounting: their felt adequacy and inference from impunity are replaced by a terminal sufficiency that assets cannot offset.

activation_trace.role: Sufficiency supplies the focus verdict that Hell alone answers the group.
Penalty supplies the consequence whose delay they misread as evidence of safety.
Failed sufficiency shows that wealth and children cannot meet or offset the divine claim.
Self-estimation supplies their false reckoning that they possess a viable standing.

structural_cues: 58:17 negates the availing force of wealth and children; 58:18 says they reckon themselves to be on something after repeating false oaths.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacent sufficiency, failed availing, and self-reckoning branches; I infer deliberate counter-accounting across them. The alternative is thematic echo without a precise reversal of their inner calculation.

changed_reading.before: Hell is simply enough punishment for their offensive speech.
changed_reading.after: حَسْبُهُمْ overturns an entire economy of false adequacy: their self-assessment, delayed-sanction test, and worldly supports all fail before one terminal sufficiency.

context_deltas.mechanism: Habitual private reciprocity can consolidate into a group bound to one opinion. The later sequence of domination, induced forgetting, and party formation supplies a social endpoint for the repeated counsel: it rehearses a shared memory regime in which divine remembrance is displaced.

activation_trace.role: Habit and continuance supply the repeated practice through which group alignment can stabilize.
Reciprocal secret counsel supplies the repeated social process that binds the participants.
Domination, seizure, and gathering supply the force that captures and consolidates the group.
Loss of remembrance supplies the displaced memory around which the captured practice operates.
A group organized around an opinion supplies the stabilized social product of repeated counsel.

structural_cues: 58:19 sequences استحوذ, فأنساهم, and حزب, moving from capture through memory loss to named faction.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies habitual counsel and a later capture-forgetting-party sequence; I infer that repeated private coordination helps produce factional identity. The alternative is direct spiritual domination unrelated to any social formation process in 58:8.

changed_reading.before: The same offenders repeatedly return to private wrongdoing.
changed_reading.after: Their repeated counsel can be read as faction-making practice: it stabilizes a shared allegiance by rehearsing speech that displaces divine remembrance.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it carries physical separation and raised-ground branches into social space. It remains anchored in the focus ن ج و and in 58:11's assembly verbs; downstream prose should present it as an exploratory spatial analogy, not as the lexical definition of نجوى.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: ن ج و at 58:8 words 7 and 13 supports both separation and elevated-ground images for a counsel that peels away from a shared assembly.

activation_trace.role: Escape by separation supplies the private group's movement out of common conversational space.
Raised ground supplies the image of an exclusionary social perch created by the counsel.
Opening width supplies the opposite assembly ethic of making shared room.
Rising and leaving a seat supplies commanded mobility rather than self-secluding elevation.
Elevation of rank relocates legitimate height from clique space to granted standing.

changed_reading.before: Secret counsel is a private exchange occurring inside an otherwise shared social setting.
changed_reading.after: It can be pictured as hostile social topography: a clique contracts common space and occupies its own perch, while the corrective assembly opens room and assigns elevation by a different rule.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is a cross-domain analogy between inward saying and writing in hearts, not an equation of نفس and قلب or of speech and script. It remains anchored in the explicit hidden utterance of 58:8 and the explicit heart-inscription of 58:22; render it as a contrast between rival inward authorizations.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: ق و ل at words 26 and 33 with ن ف س at 28 makes the group's challenge an inwardly housed utterance.

activation_trace.role: Unvoiced saying supplies the hostile proposition carried inside the speakers.
Inward intention and thought supply the receptive interior where that proposition is rehearsed.
Binding inscription supplies the contrasting image of faith fixed with authoritative force.
The heart supplies the interior site of the contrasting faithful inscription.

changed_reading.before: Their inward question is simply a thought hidden from the addressee.
changed_reading.after: The hidden question can be carried as a rival inward inscription, exposing which authority scripts allegiance inside, in contrast to faith written into hearts.

strongest_changes: The repeated return becomes specifically repairless when set against the parallel return-and-expiation sequence of 58:3.
Secret counsel loses its claim to epistemic enclosure: hearing, counting, witnessing, and knowledge turn it into an involuntary account.
58:9 and 58:12 show that private counsel is a regulable channel whose moral polarity and accountability depend on content, restraint, and an outward threshold.
58:10 identifies grief as the designed effect while bounding actual harm, revealing an intimidation mechanism.
The ح س ب and غ ن ي sequence turns Hell's sufficiency into exact counter-accounting against false self-sufficiency and self-estimation.
summary.what_was_special: The context repeatedly reuses the focus's own mechanisms rather than merely adding themes: return is contrasted with repaired return, counsel is given opposite cargo and regulated access, conventional speech becomes a shield, and sufficiency reverses self-reckoning. Long-range cues also expose possible faction-making, social topography, and rival inward inscription without forcing those exploratory readings into one synthesis.
remaining_uncertainties: The transcript model depends on treating hearing, enumeration, witness, and notification as a record mechanism rather than parallel assertions of omniscience.
The prior charity in 58:12 may function as devotional preparation rather than friction against exclusive access or capture.
The causal arrow from repeated counsel to factional identity is plausible but not explicitly stated.
The social-topography and inward-inscription readings are branch-driven analogies and should remain qualified rather than lexicalized.
